ops.title: cc-orchestrate: autobump PR merged over a failing lint check, leaving main red for 6 days
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-29 while releasing cc-orchestrate v0.17.0 as part of the daemonkit v0.23.0 fleet migration. The release lane stopped before tagging because `origin/main` was red — correctly, per the standing rule that a red run is never walked away from.

## What happened

`cc-orchestrate` PR **#1** — *"deps: daemonkit v0.23.0 — daemon state moves to ~/.daemonkit/a/<label>"* — merged on **2026-08-27** with its own `lint` check **failing**:

```
lint         fail   1m11s   .../runs/33031538822/job/98384950549
build        pass
cgo          pass
integration  pass
vuln         pass
```

Only `lint` failed; every substantive job passed. The failure was golangci-lint's **gofumpt** formatter check on test files — mechanical formatting, no behavioural content.

main then stayed red across four consecutive commits:

| sha | date | CI |
|---|---|---|
| `2971ce7` | 2026-08-24 | failure |
| `c1755ca` | 2026-08-26 | failure |
| `e628cce` | 2026-08-27 | failure |
| `de0ceac` | 2026-08-27 | failure |

The last green run on main before that was **2026-08-17** (`1ca533a`) — a six-day red window that nothing surfaced.

## Why it matters

Two compounding costs, neither hypothetical here:

1. **It blocked a release.** cc-orchestrate owns the pty daemons whose socket paths hit exactly 104 bytes under a long account name — the overflow daemonkit v0.23.0 shortened the state root to fix. Its release is what lets the dead `~/com.yasyf.cc-orchestrate/` directory be removed on every host. That release could not proceed until the lint debt was cleared first.
2. **A gate that red-lights routinely stops being read.** This is the same failure mode already recorded for the flaky Swift deadline suites: a check that is red for reasons nobody acts on trains everyone to merge past it, which is exactly how a real break hides behind an ignored signal.

## A sharp edge worth knowing

Fixing the three visible gofumpt findings surfaced a **fourth** on the next run (`orchestrate/spawn_test.go:457`). golangci-lint's `max-same-issues` default of **3** caps issues sharing one message per linter, and `File is not properly formatted (gofumpt)` is a single message — so the reported count is a floor, not a total. That cost an extra red CI cycle. The recovery is to install CI's exact toolchain and enumerate locally in one pass rather than iterating against CI.

## Fixed forward

`golangci-lint fmt` applied to `orchestrate/adoptops_test.go`, `ops_test.go`, `reconcile_test.go`, `spawn_test.go` — purely inserted blank lines plus the de-alignment that follows (`git diff -w` shows nothing). main is green again at `a451985`, and v0.17.0 released from there.

## What to decide

- Should `lint` be a **required** status check on cc-orchestrate, so a PR cannot merge over it? It was not enforced here.
- Whether the **Autobump** workflow that opened PR #1 should refuse to merge on any failing check, rather than only on the substantive ones. This PR was machine-opened and machine-merged; a human never saw the red.
- Whether to raise or remove `max-same-issues` in `.golangci.yml` so a formatter sweep reports its true total the first time.

ops.text: cc-orchestrate's lint check is either enforced as a required status check on PRs, or a deliberate decision is recorded that it should not be
The Autobump workflow's merge behaviour on a failing check is confirmed or changed
max-same-issues in cc-orchestrate's .golangci.yml is reviewed so a formatter sweep reports its full count in one pass
